current_truth_precedence: Adversarial Router Lab baseline + later synthetic design findings; no current promotion

experiments.name: Contextual competence routing baseline
experiments.result: Historical synthetic comparison reported ~64.6% for competence-aware routing vs ~58.7% for the champion/general baseline.
experiments.interpretation: Supports contextual expert selection rather than globally fixed expert trust.
experiments.notes: Retrieved from prior VECTOR context; exact generator/seed not preserved in current accessible record.

experiments.name: OOD-aware fail-open routing
experiments.result: 50,000 observations; 15% deliberate OOD contamination. Generalist 59.45%; naive specialist router 65.78%; OOD-aware fail-open router 66.36%; all deliberately injected OOD packets rejected in the reported construction.
experiments.interpretation: OOD should reduce authority and trigger fallback rather than force a nearest-expert choice.

experiments.name: False regime recurrence / deceptive similarity
experiments.result: 4,000-observation deceptive block. Generalist 56.70%; static router 46.35%; dynamic competence-veto router 56.23%; fallback on 96.3% of deceptive observations after shadow outcomes showed incompetence.
experiments.interpretation: Dormant expert recall requires state similarity AND current competence confirmation.
experiments.notes: Prevents superficial regime similarity from restoring authority.

experiments.name: Expert monopolization / concentration audit
experiments.result: Corrupted router 65.77%; arbitrary routing cap 64.57%; independent safety auditor 67.39%; healthy unbiased router 67.39%; auditor intervened on 18.6%.
experiments.interpretation: Detect unjustified concentration rather than imposing crude equalization/load balancing.

experiments.name: Checkpoint/resume determinism
experiments.result: Continuous run and process→checkpoint→stop→restore→continue produced exactly matching expert choices and final competence state in the reported test.
experiments.interpretation: Checkpoint must include learner state, support counters, calibration state, drift state, and version IDs — not only model weights.

experiments.name: Malformed/NaN fail-open injections
experiments.result: Five malformed/NaN router packet injections all followed fallback behavior without contaminating competence state.
experiments.interpretation: NaN/schema mismatch/expired TTL/missing context/unknown version/corrupt uncertainty should reject VECTOR contribution while sibling systems continue.

experiments.name: Cross-horizon propagation classification
experiments.result: 60,000-step synthetic environment. Treat-every-1m-flip: precision 6.7%, recall 100%, F1 12.6%. ≥2-horizon disagreement: precision 12.4%, recall 76.3%, F1 21.4%. Hand-built hierarchy: precision 22.5%, recall 49.3%, F1 30.9%. Learned propagation classifier: precision 68.1%, recall 66.2%, F1 67.2%, AUROC ~0.964.
experiments.interpretation: Lower-timeframe disagreement is better represented as a propagation problem than a voting problem.
experiments.notes: Synthetic generator intentionally contained learnable transition structure.

experiments.name: Cross-horizon adversarial distribution shift
experiments.result: After increasing false reversals/noise, shortening genuine lead times, and weakening confirmation: F1 fell from ~0.689 to ~0.221; AUROC fell from ~0.959 to ~0.768.
experiments.interpretation: Propagation models can become confidently obsolete; drift must decay propagation authority.

experiments.name: Propagation drift sentinel
experiments.result: MMD-style rolling monitor: 1/15 normal windows flagged, 27/27 deliberately shifted windows flagged; normal median distance 0.0023 vs shifted 0.0210.
experiments.interpretation: Cross-horizon distribution change should trigger authority reduction and revalidation.

experiments.name: Evidence-conservation duplicate attack
experiments.result: 120,000-observation environment with 8 visible observations generated by 3 latent causes. Naive aggregation: 72.34% accuracy, log loss 0.546, Brier 0.183, AUROC 0.796. Dependency-adjusted: 72.78%, 0.544, 0.182, 0.800. Adding 12 exact copies reduced naive accuracy to 68.50% and log loss to 0.592 while dependency-adjusted accuracy stayed ~72.78%; mean probability change ~0.000056.
experiments.interpretation: Repeated representation of the same information must not manufacture conviction.

experiments.name: Lineage novelty / 20-clone attack
experiments.result: 60,000 observations; 12 visible signals from 3 latent evidence families. Ordinary voting ~71.74%. After 20 copies of strongest visible signal: ~71.34%. Lineage-conserved aggregation remained ~71.74%. Adding a genuinely new fourth ~70%-reliable family raised conserved aggregation to ~75.36%.
experiments.interpretation: Clone evidence should add near-zero novelty while genuinely independent useful evidence should be able to move belief.
experiments.notes: Supports Dynamic Evidence Lineage Graph and Information Novelty Score.

experiments.name: Hidden common-cause compression
experiments.result: 80,000 observations; two latent drivers. Conventional logistic learner ~67.08% accuracy, 0.6036 log loss, 0.7343 AUROC. Common-factor compression + separate signal ~66.85%, 0.6053, 0.7317.
experiments.interpretation: Cleaner latent-factor stories do not automatically improve prediction; use soft conservation that preserves idiosyncratic residual novelty.

experiments.name: Dependency-graph staleness
experiments.result: 30,000-observation, 4-node, 3-regime system. Correct regime-specific graph one-step errors: A ~1.010, B ~1.002, C ~1.011. Keeping stale A graph: B ~1.415, C ~1.113. Using wrong B graph in C: ~1.492.
experiments.interpretation: A previously valid dependency graph can become actively harmful after structural transition.

Graph split / merge / false-recurrence / stale-graph replay
Real Icarus replay with costs/latency before any production-adjacent authority
risks: Sparse competence cells creating false certainty.
Common-mode failure if the safety auditor is too similar to the primary router.
Shadow-label latency and delayed outcome attribution.
Horizon leakage and developing higher-timeframe bar ambiguity.
Event double counting and recursive confidence inflation.
False compression of genuinely independent evidence.
Tail dependence instability and sparse tail samples.
Graph churn from over-sensitive change detection.
Causal language exceeding what observational evidence identifies.
Computational growth across asset × horizon × regime × graph versions.
Authority leakage into sibling systems if interface contracts are weakened.
